version.changelog: Add homepage, include helper scripts in bundle, clarify API domain

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pixmind-image
Version: 1.1.0

The skill exhibits a significant discrepancy between its documentation and its implementation. While SKILL.md claims the API endpoint is 'https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro', the underlying code in pixmind-api.js defaults API_BASE to 'http://127.0.0.1:8001'. This behavior causes the user's PIXMIND_API_KEY to be transmitted to a local unencrypted port by default, which could be intercepted by other local processes. Additionally, the code uses a hardcoded APP_KEY and attempts to load environment variables from a parent directory (.env), which is atypical for standalone skill bundles.

llm.summary: The skill mostly matches an image-generation purpose, but the implementation and runtime instructions diverge in ways that could leak or misroute your API key and that read undeclared local config (.env); you should verify a few mismatches before installing or running the code.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a Pixmind integration and the skill only requires PIXMIND_API_KEY — that is reasonable. However the bundled code introduces additional runtime configuration (PIXMIND_APP_KEY, PIXMIND_API_BASE) and a hard-coded APP_KEY constant, which are not documented in SKILL.md. The presence of an APP_KEY header and a configurable API_BASE are not explained by the README and are unexpected for a minimal wrapper.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md documents calls to https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro and returning CDN URLs on chatmix.top. The shipped code, however, defaults API_BASE to http://127.0.0.1:8001 and loads a .env file from the parent directory into process.env. The skill's instructions do not mention reading .env or contacting localhost; this is scope creep and a mismatch between declared runtime behavior and actual code.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is present (instruction-only with helper scripts). There is no remote download or archive extraction; risk from installation mechanism is low.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry declares only PIXMIND_API_KEY as required (primary credential). The code also uses PIXMIND_APP_KEY and PIXMIND_API_BASE (with APP_KEY defaulted to a hard-coded value and API_BASE defaulting to localhost). The code's .env loader will read a local .env and inject keys into process.env, which could expose or override other local secrets unexpectedly.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not request system-wide persistence or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but not combined with other high privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or running this skill: 1) Inspect and prefer the curl examples in SKILL.md if you only need one-off requests. 2) The shipped code defaults API_BASE to http://127.0.0.1:8001 (localhost) whereas the documentation points at https://aihub-admin.aimix.pro — confirm which endpoint you want and explicitly set PIXMIND_API_BASE to the official HTTPS endpoint if you run the scripts. 3) The code loads a .env file from the repository parent and will populate process.env for missing keys — that can pull in unrelated secrets; review any .env it would read or remove that behavior. 4) The module also sends an X-App-Key header (hard-coded fallback present) in addition to your PIXMIND_API_KEY; ask the author why this is necessary. 5) If anything is unclear, request an explanation or a version of the helper that defaults to the documented HTTPS endpoint and does not read arbitrary .env files before running. These mismatches are explainable (e.g., developer used a local test proxy), but they warrant verification before providing your API key or executing the scripts.
